feedback: Strong, near-complete capstone that catalogues essentially all ten findings with quoted evidence and defends most CVSS vectors with justifying sentences. On D1 you named all ten bugs (SQLi CWE-89, unsalted MD5 CWE-916, alg:none CWE-347, hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 CWE-798, no exp CWE-613, stored XSS CWE-79, XXE CWE-611, path traversal CWE-22, open redirect CWE-601, cookie no-Secure CWE-614) with the right CWE and a real evidence line or timestamp, which is most of the work. Several OWASP class labels were off though, XXE as A10 rather than A05, open redirect as A04 rather than A01, cookie as A07 rather than A05, and alg:none as A03 rather than A07, and since your CWEs were correct I credited those as defensible variants rather than zeroing them. The one row that cost you real points is the decoy: the intended safe construct is the HS256 verify branch using hash_equals(), which is constant-time and sound, and you never named or proved it. Saying alg:none is NOT the decoy is true, but it is not the same as identifying the actual safe construct, so the decoy row earned nothing in both D1 and D3. On D2 your chain is in order and reconciled to the capture timestamps (recon 02:14:08, failed guess 02:14:55, SQLi 02:15:31, exfil 312 rows 02:16:04, stored XSS 02:18:47, open redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02) with a verbatim PoC at each hop, and your impact section is exactly what we want, 312 customers, roughly 84 million naira, three stated assumptions, and the BoltCash launch window. The CVSS work is mostly solid with full vectors plus a sentence each, but you marked the SQLi login bypass A:H for 9.8 when it should be A:N around 9.1 because the bypass does not affect availability, and a couple of vectors lean on a reused 9.1 rather than per-finding reasoning. D3 reads well: the exec summary lands on the customers-and-naira headline and stays readable, the threat model is present, findings are tied to line numbers, the earliest-break fix correctly targets the SQLi at the first hop, your remediation is ordered by Risk Reduced Per Hour rather than raw CVSS which is exactly right, and your two detection stopgaps give a concrete field and false-positive note (request_body SQL regex, and the eyJhbGciOiJub25l base64 pattern in the Cookie header). D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice, cites ISC2 Canons I and II by numeral in a load-bearing way, anchors to your own evidence at 02:16:04, and states a clean manager-override line; the one gap is the NDPA citation, you wrote a 38-40 range and got the 72-hour NDPC trigger right under section 40 but did not cleanly name section 41 for notifying the 312 data subjects on high risk. The single most important fix is to identify and prove the real decoy, the hash_equals constant-time verify branch, instead of relitigating alg:none, because that is the row that separated this from a high-80s mark.
